solution: The sine of an angle equals the cosine of its complementary angle.

families.stem: An isosceles triangle has a base of {=base} cm and a perpendicular height of {=h} cm, drawn from the base to the opposite vertex. Find the angle at the vertex opposite the base, to the nearest degree.
solution: The height bisects the base, giving a right-angled triangle with sides {=half} cm (half the base) and {=h} cm (height).
The base angle $B$ satisfies $\tan B = \frac{{=h}}{{=half}}$, so $B = \tan^{-1}\left(\frac{{=h}}{{=half}}\right)$.
The angles of a triangle add up to $180^\circ$, so the vertex angle is $180^\circ - 2B = {=ap[t]}^\circ$ to the nearest degree.
